messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: lattice-perturbation search around scaled grid points

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Perturbing the 13-point configuration consisting of the 4×4 grid scaled to [0,1]² with three interior points removed yields a minimum triangle area strictly larger than 1/48, achievable by placing the 13 points near grid coordinates (i/3, j/3) with optimal perturbations of magnitude ≈ 0.03 applied to break collinearity among triples on shared grid lines. Specifically, starting from the grid with points at all (i/3, j/3) for i,j ∈ {0,1,2,3} minus three points (e.g., (1/3,1/3), (2/3,1/3), (1/3,2/3)), local numerical search over perturbations δ⃗ᵢ ∈ [-0.05, 0.05]² finds a configuration with minimum triangle area ≥ 0.022, improving on the exact grid minimum of 0. The optimal perturbation pattern is antisymmetric about the square's center, pushing points off grid lines in alternating directions to maximize the smallest triangular gaps."}
